answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a beacon as the anchor of the cost.
